data.title: Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs close to bagging top roles in Anthropic IPO - report
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) is said to be nearing a deal with Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) for top roles in the AI giant's blockbuster IPO.

Morgan Stanley could bag the "lead left"—the strategic adviser on the deal—role, four people familiar with the matter told the Financial Times. 

MS had held talks with potential Anthropic investors over the IPO price recently, according to two of the sources.

Goldman Sachs could be the IPO's stabilization agent. JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Citigroup (C), and Barclays (BCS) are also expected to get leading roles in the IPO, the report published on Friday noted.

The Claude chatbot owner is expected to file its IPO publicly, which could value the company over $2 trillion, as soon as next week, several sources reportedly said.

A roadshow could come near September-end, people familiar with the matter told the FT. Anthropic could begin trading in New York in late September or early October.

data.title: Sandisk leads Nasdaq's weekly gainers; Autodesk drags
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) ended flat in the red on Friday for the second straight week. Following major Wall Street indexes, the Nasdaq ended lower after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

It ended at -0.29%. For the week, the index gained 0.40%.

On a weekly basis, tech stocks dominated both the gainers and the detractors.

Sandisk (SNDK) led the gainers, with shares +17%, after a  rally driven by Dell Technologies’ stronger-than-expected second-quarter results put technology hardware stocks on a gaining spree. Strategy’s (MSTR) shares were driven higher amid a broader Bitcoin rally—gaining 12% for the week.

On the declining side, Autodesk (ADSK) occupied the top spot with shares down 16% for the week. Aerospace and defense firm Axon Enterprise (AXON) was a close second as its shares lost 14%.

data.title: The Trade Desk ends 4.5% lower, snapping a six-session winning streak
data.description:
The Trade Desk (TTD) ended 4.5% lower at $14.41 on Friday, snapping a six-session winning streak during which the stock gained 15.8%.

The stock last closed lower on Aug. 26, when it ended at $13.03.

Shares fell on Friday after the digital advertising platform said in a filing that it plans to cut roughly 15% of its workforce as part of an organizational restructuring. The headcount reductions are expected to be substantially completed in the third quarter of 2026.

The company expects to incur about $39 million to $51 million in cash restructuring and related charges, mainly for employee severance and benefits, partially offset by a $4 million to $5 million reversal related to stock-based compensation.

The stock remains down 61% year to date.

Following a second-quarter revenue miss, CEO Jeff Green said the results “did not meet the standard we set for ourselves,” citing a complex environment for marketers. The company has said it is working to improve execution and invest in artificial intelligence and measurement. In early August, the company reported second-quarter adjusted earnings of $0.34 per share, below analysts' expectations of $0.40.

data.title: KLA rises 7% amid semiconductor equipment advance
data.description:
Shares of KLA Corporation (KLAC), a supplier of process-control, inspection, and metrology equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, rallied just over 7% on Friday, closing at $185.60 after gaining $12.66 from the prior close.

The advance came amid a broader rise in the semiconductor equipment sector. Peers Applied Materials and Lam Research climbed just over 4% and just over 5%, respectively, while ASML rose just over 4%.

data.title: 3 things to look out for on Tuesday
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages finished lower on Friday after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) ended -0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) handed back -0.3%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) lost -0.2%.

The U.S. stock market will be closed Monday for observance of the Labor Day holiday.

Now, here are three things to look out for on Tuesday:

  • Nike (NKE) will hold its annual meeting. The key shareholder votes of interest will be on a proposal for a stock purchase plan expansion and a proposal on meeting environmental targets.
  • Shareholders with AtaiBeckley (ATAI) will vote on the buyout offer from Eli Lilly (LLY).
  • GameStop (GME) is slated to post second-quarter results after the closing bell. The company this past week delivered preliminary numbers.

data.title: BTC Digital clears Nasdaq bid price hurdle; shares rebound after hours
data.description:
• BTC Digital (BTCT) announced on Friday that it regained Nasdaq compliance after its closing bid price stayed at or above $1 for 10 consecutive business days.
  • The company had received a Nasdaq deficiency notice on August 27 after its shares traded below $1 for 30 consecutive business days.
  • Nasdaq confirmed the compliance and closed the matter ahead of the company’s February 23, 2027, deadline.
  • The shares closed 8.33% lower at $1.76 but gained 1.14% in after-hours trading, as investors appeared relieved by the compliance update.

data.title: U.S. drilling rig count stays flat, Baker Hughes survey says
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. remained unchanged at 588 for the third week in a row, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. rose by 2 to 449 in the week ended September 4, while gas rigs dropped by 2 to 130 and miscellaneous rigs stayed flat at 9.

The total rig count was up by 51, or 9.5%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 35, or 8.4%, from a year ago, and gas rigs gained 12, or 10.2%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin, Eagle Ford, and Williston Basin all remained unchanged at 265, 41, and 27, respectively.

data.title: Wall Street ended lower after investors received the latest payrolls print
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages finished lower after traders and investors digested the latest jobs data, which came in stronger than forecasted.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) ended -0.5%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) handed back -0.3%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) lost -0.2%. 

From a sector-by-sector standpoint, three of the 11 S&P segments closed in the green and were led by industrials. At the other end, consumer discretionary was the weakest performer. 

On the economic front, the August U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by +162K versus the +55K consensus figure, according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. At the same time, the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, compared to the 4.2% forecasted level. 

Treasury yields are on the move. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 3 basis points to 4.37%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) was higher by 1 basis point to 4.78%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) held even near 5.24%. 

“The real story is in yields. We think yields are headed down, soon, which if it happens will, we believe, push equities to new highs and attract late money into this new bull market in crypto,” Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research stated.

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of KLA Corporation (KLAC) climbed higher by +7.4%, while shares of Lululemon (LULU) fell -17.3%.

data.title: SA analyst says Treasury yields are the market’s next big catalyst
data.description:
Wall Street pulled back Friday as investors digested stronger-than-expected jobs data, while market attention increasingly turned toward Treasury yields and their potential impact on equities and cryptocurrencies.

Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research said the week’s trading showed resilience despite pressure on major indexes to break below key technical levels. 

“This week saw the major equity indices eke out modest gains after threatening to sell down below their key short-term moving averages,” King stated.

On Friday the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJI) declined -0.5%, while the S&P 500 (SP500) fell -0.3% and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) lost -0.2%. 

King noted that Bitcoin (BTC-USD) and Ether (ETH-USD) posted gains during the week, while companies holding cryptocurrencies in their treasuries significantly outperformed. Oil (CL1:COM) prices also edged higher, although futures and exchange-traded funds failed to establish a sustained upside breakout. 

“The real story is in yields,” King said, arguing that Treasury rates could become the next major catalyst for financial markets.

“We think yields are headed down, soon,” he stated, adding that falling yields could push equities to new highs while encouraging additional capital to enter the cryptocurrency market. 

King said such a move could ultimately attract “late money into this new bull market in crypto,” reinforcing his constructive outlook despite Friday’s market decline.

data.title: September Fed hike 'wouldn't be the worst thing' for stocks - Citi's Chronert
data.description:
Citi analyst Scott Chronert said Friday a preemptive Federal Reserve rate hike in September "wouldn't be the worst thing" for equity markets (SPY) (DIA) (QQQ). Given elevated concerns about the Fed's next move, Chronert believes markets would likely look through such an action and view it somewhat positively—though the critical question becomes whether investors are facing one or two hikes, or the start of an entirely new rate-hiking cycle.

While Citi is not overly concerned about a full-blown rate-hiking cycle materializing, Chronert emphasized that equity valuations critically depend on stability at the long end of the yield curve (TLT) (TLH) (ZROZ). "What I do need is a stable back end of the curve to support the valuation setup," he told CNBC in an interview, noting his team is focused squarely on where the 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) is headed rather than obsessing over Fed funds alone.

Chronert is maintaining his 8,100 year-end S&P 500 (SP500) price target, which would require roughly one percent monthly gains through year-end. He expects Q3 earnings season to provide fundamental support for equities. Beyond that, navigating the midterm elections should give way to a relief rally opportunity that sets up a positive path into December. The AI (AIQ) (AIEQ) narrative, he added, continues to unfold more positively than not.

On mega-cap (MGC) growth and technology (XLK), Chronert acknowledged a mixed third quarter so far—tech in aggregate has been roughly a market performer, but that result masks a software (IGV) surge offset by a semiconductor (SMH) selloff. The mega-cap growth cohort, representing 35% to 50% of the index depending on measurement, has delivered uneven performance and influence on broader index action. 

Looking ahead, Chronert expects this group to find its footing as confidence builds around the persistence of the AI investment theme into 2027 and beyond, supporting continued market breadth. "That fundamental picture still net-net is pretty constructive," he said.
